## 2.2.1: \[Mendeley Data\]

**Producer and authority.** \[This dataset was published by Mendeley data, which is an online research data repository. They used this platform to publish and share datasets. The dataset comes from a research study involving Brazillian schoolchildren and follows certain protocols and ethical standards. However any kind of research grant or funding could not be accessed through this webpage. The datasets author is flavia Schaidhauer. \]

**Original Dataset Purpose.** \[This was to investigate a childs reltionship between daily screen time, social media use and depressive symptoms and how it was associated to their mental health.\]

**Collection method.** \[The data was collected through a cross-sectional study involving 320 school children in brazil between the year of 2024 to 2025 regarding information about their screen time, social media usage and physical activity. However, our dataset does not explicitly explain how it was retrieved either from students or their devices directly.\]

**Coverage and resolution.** \[This dataset covers 320 Brazillian school children between the year of 2024 to 2025. its coverage is in brazil although the exact place city or date is not specefied in this dataset. The dataset is cross-sectional which means that they represent observations collected during a specefic study period and not annual measurements over time. And each row represents one child its different variables related to it.\]

**Licence.** \[This dataset is published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence.\]

**Access.** \[I accessed this dataset on the Mendeley Data website https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/h27yvy7986/2 which is publicly available for everyone to access and its CSV files are also easily accessible and downloadable.\]

**Known problems.** \[After examining the CSV and the excel files there was not alot of inconsistency but there were some missing values and the dataset has 320 observations and not every supported full set of information.\]

```{r source-1-load}
 {r source-1-load}

#loading the required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

#loading the raw and unfiltered mendeley dataset
 raw_1 <- read_csv("data/raw/dataset_depressao_infantil_public.csv") # example for a csv file
 glimpse(raw_1) |> select(1:6) 
```

## 2.2.2 \[Average Daily Screen Time for Children\]

**Producer and authority.** \[This dataset was uploaded to kaggle by one of its users where different individuals upload datasets for educational purposes. As it is not a publically verified website it does not have a specefic grant or mandate.\]

**Original Dataset Purpose.** \[ This datasets original purpose was to determine the childs average daily screen time and how it is different depending on their age, gender and there screen usage in different areas.\]

**Collection method.** \[ The original method of the datasets collection is not mentioned in the CSV file. It is not clear whether the data came from surveys, real life data collection or other methods.

**Coverage and resolution.** \[ The dataset covers children from the age of 5-15 years and it contains variables such as gender, age, screen time and its different types and the day type weekdays or weekend.
